_readme: THE WORLD (2026-10-21): the one atlas every scene stands on. Mark: "Data sets should never be
specific to place, only the measurement type", and "make sure you wrap up making everything part
of a global model". This file holds each measurement's global set -- the water composite of
harvest/fidelity/world.gafid (bed, tides, currents, sea state, rivers), the ETOPO 15" folder,
the planet's buildings, roads and bridges, the OSM coast and inland water -- and the laws, layers and
closures, and NO place. A place is a scene on top of it (scenes/merrimack.json, demos/mavericks.json,
demos/tokyo.json): its anchor, its views, its solver's box and its wave field's window. Where a river
meets a place's solver, where its tide and its datum link come from, which buildings stand there: the
data says, by measurement, for any box anywhere.
Sections, keys and units: src/scene/SceneSchema.h. Resolution: defaults < this file < includes
< a scene that names this one as base < --set; objects by key, named arrays by name, placements
replaced whole (SceneBuilder.h). data/wave_scene.json overlays `water` (the M8 water scene's closures).

data._atlas: ONE ATLAS (2026-10-21, Mark: "Data sets should never be specific to place, only the measurement type"): every dataset here is a measurement's global set -- the water composite of harvest/fidelity/world.gafid (bed, tides, currents, sea state, river gauges), the planet's buildings, roads and bridges -- and every scene that inherits this one flies the same world. A scene chooses a place (place.anchor, views, the solver's box, the wave field's window); it names no data of its own.

streaming._seafloor: Off (Mark, 2026-10-11): the seafloor relief paints a made-up sediment ramp, and at a coarse tile it stair-stepped sand over the coast. No fake colours for now.
streaming._gisLand: THE GLOBAL COAST, every scene that inherits this one: OSM's land polygons of 2026-10-11 (harvester/harvest_land_polygons.py). Without it a place outside New England had no survey and its shore was a coarse height test.
streaming._gisWater: THE PLANET'S INLAND WATER (2026-10-21): OSM's water polygons classed sea, impounded and reach (harvester/harvest_osm_water.py), in place of New England's NHD carve -- rivers, lakes and marsh channels everywhere a scene flies.

views.name: orbit
views._at: the globe start: over the North Atlantic at 2.1 planet radii, aimed at the centre

sources.name: noaa.inlethq
sources._over: the hydrographic survey stands OVER the 2018 lidar where both have a bottom: in the turbid channel a laser return can be the water's surface, a 2025 sounding is the better witness; the lidar keeps the beach and the bars the survey never saw. The survey itself stood +3 m too high until 2026-10-17 evening (eHydro depths taken as heights). Its `feather` fades its weight from every nodata edge (the land BlueTopo never covered) as from its box.
